controlled_change: Offline SLRU versus CLOCK at equal aligned bytes over committed routes from the normal mixed-reference coding request.
correctness: All 32 decode forwards and 1,584 layer passes were captured and matched to request inputs and outputs. Native tests and independent trace-reader checks passed; no new independent full-model logit or coding-quality qualification.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: The 32-step fixed-order simulation suggests 10.71 percent fewer decode expert reads; normal-request latency benefit remains unmeasured.
hypothesis: A probation/protected cache could reduce decode expert reads at the observed 1,848-slot allocation.
limitations: Retrospective interpretation of one short instrumented request.
This is simulated read reduction, not measured speedup; no production default changes.
Fixed-order simulation omits live GPU leases, native hit-first admission and memory-compression cost.
outcome: Normal capture finished in 33.97 seconds. Instrumented generation was 2.42 tokens per second. At actual capacity, simulated CLOCK missed 14,236 times versus 14,221 native misses; SLRU simulated 13,535 total misses. Process compression was observed; system swap did not grow during this request.
smallest_experiment: Extend the deadline-limited locality capture to 256 decode steps and a retained-history append, then screen one cache policy at equal admitted memory if the read benefit persists.
